subs.label: Historical & Period Film
subs.axis: Axis: by the representational mode of the past: epic spectacle by era first, then national period traditions, literary costume film, and last the reconstruction of real political, social and documented events.

leaves.label: Historical Epic
leaves.defn: A large-scale, long-form spectacle that sweeps a nation, dynasty or family through decades of real history, with the historical upheaval itself as the subject (Intolerance, Gone with the Wind, 1900, Ponniyin Selvan: Part I). Ancient Mediterranean spectacles go to A8-2; epics built around a battle campaign go to A9-1.
leaves.see: A8-2 Sword-and-Sandal Film; A9-1 War Epic
leaves.axis: by setting, foundation sagas first, ancient and pre-contact worlds last

leaves.label: Sword-and-Sandal Film
leaves.defn: A spectacle set in Greco-Roman or biblical antiquity, built on gladiators, legions, mythic heroes or Old Testament stories (Ben-Hur, Spartacus, The Ten Commandments, 300). Lives of Jesus and the saints go to A11-4 Religious Biopic.
leaves.see: A11-4 Religious Biopic; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
leaves.axis: by source world: Old and New Testament, Rome, Greek myth

leaves.label: Medieval Film
leaves.defn: A film set in the European or Near Eastern Middle Ages whose world of knights, sagas, crusades and feudal law is the subject rather than a single battle campaign (The Northman, The Last Duel, Flesh+Blood, Arn: The Knight Templar). Battle-centred medieval epics go to A9-1.
leaves.see: A9-1 War Epic; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Royal Court Drama
leaves.defn: A period drama of intrigue inside a royal or imperial court, where succession, favour and palace politics drive the story and no single royal life is traced (The Lion in Winter, Queen Margot, Curse of the Golden Flower, The King's Warden). A film tracing a monarch's life goes to A11-1 Royal Biopic.
leaves.see: A11-1 Royal Biopic; B4 Chinese-Language Drama

leaves.label: Jidaigeki
leaves.defn: A Japanese period drama set before the Meiji Restoration in which manners, clan duty and social hierarchy, not sword combat, carry the story (Sansho the Bailiff, Rashomon, Ran, The Twilight Samurai). A film driven by swordplay goes to A8-6 Chanbara.

leaves.label: Chanbara
leaves.defn: A Japanese swordplay film in which sword combat by samurai or ronin is the engine of the drama (Yojimbo, Seven Samurai, The Tale of Zatoichi, 13 Assassins). Swordless period dramas go to A8-5 Jidaigeki.
leaves.see: A8-5 Jidaigeki; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by series and era: classic ronin films, the Zatoichi series, the Lone Wolf and Cub revenge cycle, modern revival
secs: Lone Wolf and Cub & Revenge Manga Films

leaves.label: Colonial & Slavery Film
leaves.defn: A period film whose subject is chattel slavery or colonial rule and resistance to it, told from the plantation, the mission or the colony (Burn!, The Last Supper, 12 Years a Slave, The Camp at Thiaroye). Battle-centred colonial wars go to A9-1.
leaves.see: A9-1 War Epic; A1 Movements & Schools (Third Cinema)
leaves.axis: by system: slavery and abolition first, colonial rule and revolt second

leaves.label: Heritage Film
leaves.defn: A British (or British-set) period film of gentility, country houses and pre-war manners, usually from a classic English novel, valued for its nostalgic re-creation of the national past (A Room with a View, Pride & Prejudice, Howards End, Downton Abbey). Continental and American literary costume films go to A8-9.
leaves.axis: by literary period: Austen first, then Georgian and Victorian novels, Edwardian, and the interwar country house

leaves.label: Costume Drama
leaves.defn: A period drama, usually adapted from a classic novel or play, whose dress, manners and social codes of a past society are the dramatic material (Les Misérables, The Leopard, Anna Karenina, Portrait of a Lady on Fire). British gentility films go to A8-8 Heritage Film.
leaves.axis: by literary tradition of the source, original screenplays and twentieth-century pieces last

leaves.label: Shakespeare Film
leaves.defn: A screen adaptation of a Shakespeare play, in period or transposed dress, with the play's text and structure carrying it (Hamlet, Chimes at Midnight, Henry V, The Tragedy of Macbeth). Free transpositions into another culture such as Throne of Blood stay with their tradition.

leaves.label: Political Drama
leaves.defn: A period drama of private lives under a named political regime, where dictatorship, purge, occupation or revolution is the pressure that shapes the story (Mephisto, Burnt by the Sun, No, A Taxi Driver). Dramatised single events go to A8-13 Docudrama; lives of politicians go to A11-2.
leaves.axis: by regime: fascism first, Stalinism, Latin American juntas, other twentieth-century histories, earlier revolutions last

leaves.label: Social Problem Film
leaves.defn: A period drama that dramatises a social injustice of its era, such as labour, emigration, women's rights, race, sexuality or persecution, through fictional representative lives (Germinal, Vera Drake, The Help, The Crucible). Real activists' lives go to A11-2.
leaves.axis: by the social question: labour first, then emigration, women, race, queer history, religious persecution last

leaves.label: Docudrama
leaves.defn: A dramatised reconstruction of one documented real event, crisis or case, where the event rather than a person's life is the subject (A Night to Remember, Apollo 13, United 93, The Post). A film tracing a person's life goes to A11.
leaves.aliases: based on a true story, drama-documentary
leaves.axis: by the kind of event: disasters and expeditions, political crises, massacres and terror, legal cases, journalism, humanitarian crises

subs.label: War Film
subs.axis: Axis: by war in chronological order (pre-modern battles to the War on Terror), then by mode (aftermath, anti-war).

leaves.label: War Epic
leaves.defn: A large-scale battle spectacle of a pre-twentieth-century war or an early-twentieth-century revolution, with the campaign as the narrative spine (Alexander Nevsky, Braveheart, Zulu, Glory). WWI and later go to their own leaves.
leaves.see: A8-1 Historical Epic; A8-3 Medieval Film
leaves.axis: by era: ancient and medieval, early modern and colonial, American wars, twentieth-century revolutions and civil wars
secs: Revolutions & Civil Wars of the Early 20th Century

leaves.label: World War I Film
leaves.defn: A film of the First World War, its trenches, air war and immediate aftermath (All Quiet on the Western Front, Paths of Glory, Gallipoli, 1917).
leaves.see: A9-14 Anti-War Film; A9-13 Returning Veteran Film

leaves.label: World War II Combat Film
leaves.defn: A combat film of the Second World War in Europe and the Mediterranean, centred on soldiers, aircrews or sailors in action (Saving Private Ryan, Das Boot, The Guns of Navarone, Come and See is A9-5). Pacific theatre goes to A9-4.
leaves.see: A9-4 Pacific War Film; A9-5 Partisan & Resistance Film
leaves.axis: by front and mode: Western Front, air and sea, commando missions, Eastern Front, Nordic fronts

leaves.label: Pacific War Film
leaves.defn: A film of the Pacific and Asian theatres of the Second World War, including the Second Sino-Japanese War (The Burmese Harp, The Human Condition, Letters from Iwo Jima, The Thin Red Line). POW camps go to A9-7.
leaves.see: A9-7 Prisoner-of-War Film; A9-9 Atomic Bomb Film

leaves.label: Partisan & Resistance Film
leaves.defn: A film of irregular fighters and resistance networks against occupation in the Second World War, with the Yugoslav partisan film as its named canon (The Battle of Neretva, Walter Defends Sarajevo, The Ascent, Army of Shadows). Old leaf Partisan Film merged here with resistance films.
leaves.see: A9-3 World War II Combat Film; A9-6 Holocaust Film
leaves.axis: by region: the Yugoslav cycle first, Soviet and East European partisans, Western European resistance

leaves.label: Holocaust Film
leaves.defn: A fiction film of the Nazi persecution and murder of European Jews: camps, ghettos, deportations, hiding and the reckoning afterwards (Schindler's List, The Pianist, Son of Saul, The Zone of Interest).
leaves.see: A9-5 Partisan & Resistance Film; A19 Documentary
leaves.axis: by the site of persecution: camps, ghettos and round-ups, hiding and rescue, perpetrators and aftermath

leaves.label: Prisoner-of-War Film
leaves.defn: A war film set among captured soldiers in a POW camp, built on survival, collaboration or escape (Stalag 17, The Great Escape, The Bridge on the River Kwai, Rescue Dawn).
leaves.see: A9-3 World War II Combat Film; A2 Crime (prison film)

leaves.label: Home Front Film
leaves.defn: A war film centred on civilians, families and children living through a war away from or overrun by the front (Mrs. Miniver, Forbidden Games, Two Women, Empire of the Sun).
leaves.see: A9-13 Returning Veteran Film; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by war and viewpoint: world-war home fronts, children in war, civilians in later wars

leaves.label: Atomic Bomb Film
leaves.defn: A Japanese film of the atomic bombings and the hibakusha who survived them (Black Rain).

leaves.label: Vietnam War Film
leaves.defn: A film of the Vietnam War, American or Vietnamese, in combat or in its training camps (Platoon, Full Metal Jacket, Wild Field, Da 5 Bloods). Veterans' homecoming goes to A9-13.
leaves.see: A9-13 Returning Veteran Film; A9-14 Anti-War Film

leaves.label: Modern War Film
leaves.defn: A film of a post-1945 war other than Vietnam and the War on Terror: Korea, decolonisation, the Balkans, the Middle East, insurgencies and Ukraine (Tae Guk Gi, No Man's Land, Lebanon, Beasts of No Nation).
leaves.see: A9-12 War on Terror Film; A9-10 Vietnam War Film
leaves.axis: by conflict, roughly chronological: Korea and the Cold War, African wars, Balkans and Caucasus, Middle East, insurgencies, Ukraine, Afghanistan and South Asia

leaves.label: War on Terror Film
leaves.defn: A film of the Gulf, Iraq and Afghanistan wars and counter-terror operations after 1990, often built on a single real mission (The Hurt Locker, Black Hawk Down, Jarhead, Warfare).
leaves.aliases: Iraq War film, Afghanistan War film
leaves.see: A9-11 Modern War Film; A3 Thriller & Mystery

leaves.label: Returning Veteran Film
leaves.defn: A film of a war's aftermath for those who fought or occupied: homecoming, trauma, mine-clearing and reckoning (The Best Years of Our Lives, Birdy, Land of Mine, Beanpole). Weakly attested label; the field also says homecoming film.
leaves.see: A9-8 Home Front Film; A16 Drama

leaves.label: Anti-War Film
leaves.defn: A film whose primary mode is protest against war itself, by allegory or by satire, rather than depiction of one campaign (Johnny Got His Gun, Shame, Three Kings, Jojo Rabbit).
leaves.axis: by mode: allegory and protest, satire and comedy

subs.label: Western
subs.axis: Axis: by the western's historical cycle and its transpositions: silent and classical forms first, then revisionist and European cycles, transposed and contemporary westerns last.

leaves.label: Silent Western
leaves.defn: A western of the silent era, from William S. Hart to John Ford's first epics (Hell's Hinges, The Iron Horse, The Wind).

leaves.label: Classical Western
leaves.defn: A Hollywood sound western of the studio era and its later classical survivors, built on the frontier code of lawmen, cattlemen, cavalry and gunfighters (Stagecoach, The Searchers, Rio Bravo, Winchester '73). Westerns that interrogate the myth go to A10-6.
leaves.axis: by story type: cavalry and epic, lawman and town-tamer, range and homestead, psychological revenge, Mexico-border mercenaries

leaves.label: Singing Cowboy Western
leaves.defn: A B-western musical vehicle for a singing cowboy star (Under Western Stars, Melody Ranch).

leaves.label: Comedy Western
leaves.defn: A western played for comedy or parody of the frontier code (Go West, Destry Rides Again, Cat Ballou, Shanghai Noon).

leaves.label: Musical Western
leaves.defn: A stage or screen musical set on the frontier (Calamity Jane, Oklahoma!, Seven Brides for Seven Brothers).

leaves.label: Revisionist Western
leaves.defn: A western that questions the frontier myth, its violence, heroes, racial and gender order (The Wild Bunch, McCabe & Mrs. Miller, Unforgiven, Meek's Cutoff).
leaves.see: A10-2 Classical Western; A10-7 Acid Western
leaves.axis: by what is revised: the myth itself, the outlaw, race and Native America, frontier women and settlers

leaves.label: Acid Western
leaves.defn: A countercultural, hallucinatory western of the late 1960s and its descendants (The Shooting, El Topo, Dead Man).

leaves.label: Spaghetti Western
leaves.defn: An Italian-produced western of the 1960s–70s cycle, with its operatic violence and its Trinity comic offshoot (A Fistful of Dollars, Django, The Great Silence, They Call Me Trinity).

leaves.label: Ostern
leaves.defn: An Eastern Bloc western, East German Indianerfilm or Soviet "red western" (The Sons of Great Bear, Apaches, Nobody Wanted to Die).

leaves.label: Meat Pie Western
leaves.defn: An Australian western of bushrangers and the outback frontier (The Story of the Kelly Gang, Ned Kelly, The Proposition).

leaves.label: Transnational Western
leaves.defn: A western whose codes are transposed to another nation's landscape and history, from Manchuria to Patagonia (The Good, the Bad, the Weird, Marlina the Murderer in Four Acts, The Settlers, Bacurau). Italian and Eastern Bloc cycles have their own leaves. Weakly attested umbrella label.

leaves.label: Neo-Western
leaves.defn: A film set in the contemporary American West in which the western's codes of land, law and violence persist (Hud, No Country for Old Men, Hell or High Water, Wind River).

subs.label: Biographical Film
subs.axis: Axis: by the field in which the subject is known: power (royals, politics, war, religion), discovery (exploration, science, business), the arts (visual, literary, music, show business), sport, crime, and private lives last.

leaves.label: Royal Biopic
leaves.defn: A film tracing the life or reign of a monarch, consort or royal favourite (The Private Life of Henry VIII, Sissi, The King's Speech, Spencer). Court intrigue without a single life goes to A8-4.
leaves.see: A8-4 Royal Court Drama; A11-2 Political Biopic
leaves.axis: by dynasty and region: England to the Stuarts, Britain from the Georgians, continental courts, Asian rulers

leaves.label: Political Biopic
leaves.defn: A film tracing the life or career of a statesman, revolutionary, activist or dissident (Gandhi, Malcolm X, Lincoln, Milk). A single political crisis goes to A8-13 Docudrama.
leaves.axis: by role: rulers and statesmen, revolutionaries, civil-rights activists, journalists and whistleblowers

leaves.label: Military Biopic
leaves.defn: A film tracing the life of a soldier, general or war hero, where the person rather than one battle is the subject (Sergeant York, Lawrence of Arabia, El Cid, Napoleon). Battle-centred true stories go to A9.

leaves.label: Religious Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of the life of Jesus, a prophet, saint, reformer or religious leader (The Gospel According to St. Matthew, The Passion of the Christ, Kundun, The Message). Old Testament spectacles go to A8-2.

leaves.label: Explorer & Adventurer Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of an explorer, mountaineer or solitary adventurer, where the journey into the unknown is the life (Dersu Uzala, Into the Wild, The Lost City of Z, Tenzing).
leaves.see: A11-12 Sports Biopic; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Science & Medicine Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a scientist, physician, inventor or astronaut, built on the discovery and its cost (A Beautiful Mind, The Imitation Game, Oppenheimer, First Man).
leaves.axis: by field: science and mathematics, medicine, invention and engineering, space flight

leaves.label: Business Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of an entrepreneur, tycoon or company founding, built on the rise and the deal (The Social Network, The Aviator, The Founder, BlackBerry). Fraudsters go to A11-13.

leaves.label: Artist Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a painter, sculptor, photographer, fashion designer or dancer, built around the making of the work (Rembrandt, Frida, Mr. Turner, Saint Laurent).
leaves.axis: by medium: painting, photography, fashion and dance

leaves.label: Writer Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a novelist, poet, playwright or thinker, built around the writing and the life that fed it (Becoming Jane, Capote, Bright Star, Tolkien). Adaptations of a writer's own memoir of ordinary life go to A11-14.
leaves.see: A11-14 Autobiographical & Memoir Film; A11-8 Artist Biopic
leaves.axis: by literary era, children's authors last

leaves.label: Musical Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a composer, singer, band or performer, with the music performed as part of the story (Amadeus, Ray, Walk the Line, Bohemian Rhapsody).
leaves.see: A14 Musical & Dance Film; A11-11 Show Business Biopic
leaves.axis: by musical tradition: classical, jazz and soul, rock and pop, country and folk, hip hop, chanson and world popular music

leaves.label: Show Business Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a stage, film or television entertainer, filmmaker or impresario, built on the business of performing (Chaplin, Ed Wood, Judy, Man on the Moon).
leaves.axis: by stage: theatre and vaudeville, Hollywood, television and comedy, world film industries

leaves.label: Sports Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of an athlete, coach or team, built on a career rather than a single match (Ali, Foxcatcher, I, Tonya, The Iron Claw).
leaves.axis: by sport: combat sports, team sports, individual and endurance sports

leaves.label: Crime Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a real gangster, outlaw, swindler, killer or militant, built on the criminal career (GoodFellas, Catch Me If You Can, Monster, Carlos).
leaves.axis: by kind of crime: organised crime, robbery and fraud, murder cases, political violence

leaves.label: Autobiographical & Memoir Film
leaves.defn: A film adapted from a memoir or tracing the true life of a private person, known for what they lived through rather than a public field (My Left Foot, Angela's Ashes, Girl, Interrupted, Lion). Weakly attested umbrella label.
leaves.axis: by the life experience: family and self-discovery, addiction and mental illness, illness and disability, trauma and survival, teachers, couples
